Read the transcript of the audio guide
  1. On a December afternoon in 1891, a young Canadian instructor nailed two peach baskets to the balcony rails of a Springfield gymnasium and handed his restless students a new game. source
  2. He had invented basketball — and he was not yet an American. source
  3. James Naismith was born on 6 November 1861 in Ramsay Township, in what was then Upper Canada, near the town of Almonte, Ontario. source
  4. By the early 1890s he was a physical instructor at the International YMCA Training School in Springfield, Massachusetts. source
  5. Two instructors had already given up on the class. source
  6. Naismith was given two weeks to solve it. source
  7. Naismith wanted a game of skill rather than brute force — one where you could not run with the ball or tackle the man who had it. source
  8. He wrote out thirteen rules, asked a janitor for two boxes, and was handed two peach baskets instead. source
  9. The first game, in December 1891, was played with a soccer ball and the baskets, nine players a side. source
  10. It did not go smoothly. source
  11. In January 1939, in an interview on the radio, James Naismith said this about the very first game: source
  12. The boys began tackling, kicking and punching in the clinches. They ended up in a free-for-all in the middle of the gym floor. source
  13. But the game spread with astonishing speed through the YMCA network, and the rules were published in 1892. source
  14. Basketball was played at the 1936 Berlin Games, and Naismith was there to see it. source
  15. He filed for American citizenship near the end of the First World War, and the grant came in 1925 — when he was sixty-three years old and had been teaching in the country for more than three decades. source
  16. What makes someone belong to a country: the work they do there, or a piece of paper?
